sections.heading: Remembering who you are and admitting what I am
sections.text:
Father, you made everything and you hold everything together. The rhythm of day and night belongs to you. The sky above me and the ground under my feet keep speaking of your greatness.

And still, I have sinned against you. I have pushed back against what my conscience knew was right. I have treated your commands as if they were optional. I have heard the good news of Christ and still resisted its call on my life. Yet you have not left me without hope. You have given me a real hope in your mercy, and I come to you because of it.
theological_themes: God is Creator and Sustainer of all things; creation displays his glory.
Sin is not merely weakness but resistance to conscience, God's law, and the gospel.
The believer approaches God through hope given by grace, not through personal worthiness.

scripture_references.connection: This passage presents creation as a continual witness to God's glory, which grounds the prayer's opening awareness that heaven and earth belong to God and declare his greatness.
Paul teaches that conscience bears witness to moral reality, which supports the confession that sin can involve resisting what one knows inwardly to be right.
Peter describes believers as born again to a living hope through Christ's resurrection, matching the prayer's confidence that even confessed sin is met under God's given hope.

sections.heading: Asking to want holiness more than the world
sections.text:
Please pull my heart away from the attitudes and desires that belong to this passing world. You have given me new birth from above, and my future is with you in glory. So teach me to see holiness not as a burden, but as the true beauty of a soul made alive by you.

Make me want what is clean, true, and pleasing to you. Let holiness become something I love, not merely something I know I should choose.
theological_themes: New birth changes a person's identity and direction.
Because the believer belongs to the coming glory, worldly desires must be resisted.
Holiness is not merely duty but the fitting beauty of a life restored to God.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus teaches that entrance into God's kingdom requires being born from above by the Spirit, which supports the prayer's appeal to a new identity and new desires.
Paul connects union with the risen Christ and future glory with seeking the things above rather than living by earthly desires.
Peter calls believers, as obedient children, not to be shaped by former passions but to be holy because God is holy, directly grounding this request for holiness.

sections.heading: Staying awake in a dangerous world
sections.text:
Do not let me drift into spiritual sleep. Keep me from becoming careless, dull, or comfortable with sin. Guard the assurance you have given me, and when it grows weak, draw me back to what is true in Christ.

I am walking through enemy territory, so help me not to move through life unarmed. Keep me alert to temptation, lies, pride, fear, and whatever would pull me away from you. Teach me to depend on the protection you provide, not on my own strength.
theological_themes: The Christian life requires vigilance because temptation and spiritual opposition are real.
Assurance is a gift to be guarded by returning to God's promises in Christ.
God provides spiritual armor for believers who cannot stand in their own strength.

scripture_references.connection: Paul commands believers to be strong in the Lord and to put on God's armor because spiritual opposition is real, which directly supports the prayer's request to remain armed in enemy territory.
Peter warns Christians to be sober-minded and watchful against the devil's hostility, grounding the prayer's plea not to become spiritually sleepy or careless.
Paul describes the Spirit bearing witness that believers are God's children, which supports the prayer's concern that assurance be preserved and renewed by God.

sections.heading: Trusting you in every circumstance
sections.text:
Make me ready for whatever you place in front of me. When life is ordinary, keep me faithful. When life is painful, keep my mind steady on you. When trials come, do not let them be wasted in me.

Use hardship to humble me, deepen me, and teach me gratitude. Help me see, even if only later, how you are working through what I would never have chosen. Let my difficulties lead me to praise you for your wisdom and care.
theological_themes: God is able to fit his people for every circumstance they face.
Trials can become instruments of growth under God's providence.
A mind fixed on God can remain steady even in trouble.

scripture_references.connection: Isaiah speaks of God keeping in peace the one whose mind is stayed on him, which supports the request for a steady mind in changing circumstances.
Paul teaches that God works all things for the good of those who love him, with the goal of conforming them to Christ, grounding the prayer's hope that trials can become blessings by God's design.
James explains that testing produces steadfastness and maturity, which supports the prayer's desire that hardship not be wasted but used to form the believer.

sections.heading: Letting your truth reshape my obedience
sections.text:
Straighten out the way I think. Let your truth become clear to me, consistent in me, and strong enough to change how I live. Do not let me pick and choose from your revealed will.

Teach me to value the whole gospel—its promises and its commands. I do not want to admire grace while ignoring obedience, or obey outwardly while forgetting grace. Make doing your will feel less like forced compliance and more like the free, glad response of a child who trusts his Father.
theological_themes: God's revealed truth must shape both belief and practice.
The gospel includes both promises to receive and commands to obey.
Christian obedience is meant to become holy, sincere, and joyful rather than merely external.

scripture_references.connection: Paul teaches that all Scripture is God-breathed and equips God's people for every good work, supporting the prayer's refusal to undervalue any part of God's revealed will.
Paul presents grace as both saving and training believers to renounce ungodliness and live upright lives, which fits the prayer's concern to hold together gospel promises and gospel obedience.
Jesus connects love for him with keeping his commandments, grounding the prayer's desire for obedience that is relational and sincere rather than merely formal.

sections.heading: Living faithfully in prosperity, suffering, and ordinary duties
sections.text:
Set me apart for you in every relationship, responsibility, conversation, decision, and season of life. If things go well for me, keep me from becoming proud or self-important. If I suffer, keep sorrow from swallowing me whole.

Give me a balanced heart in changing circumstances. Help me receive every duty—not as an interruption, not as a way to prove myself, but as a spiritual privilege before you. Make me content in you, useful to others, and a life that brings honor to your name.
theological_themes: Sanctification touches every part of life, not only private devotion.
Prosperity brings the danger of pride, and suffering brings the danger of despair.
Contentment and faithful duty can glorify God and serve as an example to others.

scripture_references.connection: Paul describes learning contentment in both abundance and need through Christ's strength, directly supporting the prayer's desire for balance in prosperity and suffering.
Paul teaches that even ordinary actions are to be done for God's glory, which grounds the prayer's request to honor God in every duty and circumstance.
Paul urges Timothy to be an example in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity, which supports the prayer's hope to become a faithful example to others.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original assumes a robust doctrine of providence in which trials have divine design and can become blessings. Some readers may find this pastorally difficult, especially in severe suffering; the adaptation preserves the claim while avoiding any suggestion that pain itself is good or that grief should be minimized.

The phrase 'bound for glory' reflects confidence in the believer's final salvation. The adaptation preserves this as Christian hope while still allowing for the prayer's concern that assurance may weaken and need to be guarded.

The original's language about 'enemy land' reflects spiritual warfare imagery. The adaptation keeps the concrete image while clarifying that the enemy includes temptation, lies, sin, and spiritual opposition rather than people as enemies.
significant_interpretive_choices: 'Worldly dispositions' was rendered as attitudes and desires belonging to the passing world, to preserve the moral and spiritual contrast without making ordinary created life sound evil in itself.
'Holiness as the beauty and dignity of the soul' was interpreted not as aesthetic refinement or social respectability, but as the fitting beauty of a life restored to God.

'Rectify all my principles' was rendered as God straightening out the way I think, because the original is asking for deep correction of convictions and motives by divine truth, not merely better opinions.

'Every relation, office, transaction and condition of life' was broadened into relationships, responsibilities, conversations, decisions, and seasons of life, to carry the original's comprehensive scope into contemporary language.
